fact_text: UBL's total deposits roughly doubled from about 3 trillion rupees at June 2024 to about 6 trillion in the latest reported figures, implying about 40 percent annual growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In UBL's latest reported deposit mix, current accounts were about 55 percent of total deposits, but local-currency deposits alone were below 50 percent, because foreign-currency deposits are a large part of the total.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Between June 2024 and March 2026 UBL's foreign-currency deposits grew faster than its local deposits, so the growth quality of the deposit base is weaker than the headline figure suggests.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Current-account deposits pay zero interest, so a higher current-account share lowers funding cost and raises the spread a bank earns; that is why the analyst watches the current-account ratio closely.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dollar loans are common to oil refiners and marketing companies that open letters of credit abroad, and they earn a narrower spread than rupee lending on local deposits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: At roughly 20 percent of industry deposits, a bank that is already the market leader finds it nearly impossible to double deposits in two years, so its share gains slow down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A bank's deposit growth must beat the sector's natural growth, which tracks money-supply growth, to gain market share; the analyst treats deposit growth as the key driver of bank earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An IMF programme condition bars the central bank from lending directly to the government, so the government borrows indirectly: banks borrow from the central bank through open market operations and lend the money on to the government, keeping a margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In 2024, with policy rates starting near 19 percent, UBL borrowed heavily from the central bank and lent to the government on one- and two-year tenors at about 18 to 19 percent; as its funding cost fell, the carry widened.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL's long-term government floating PIBs reprice every six months at six-month KIBOR plus about 75 basis points, so the spread is fixed while the base rate moves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Banking profits face an effective tax rate of roughly 50 percent, so the pre-tax carry on government lending is about halved by the time it reaches earnings per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The government paid banks an incentive to bring in remittances; UBL received about 3.5 billion rupees of it in 2025, and the analyst notes the incentive has since been stopped, so banks absorb those costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Losing the 2025-sized remittance incentive would cut UBL's after-tax earnings by only about 1 rupee per share, which the analyst considers not meaningful.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam,'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL has a large Middle East lending book, and a worsening regional conflict could turn some of those loans non-performing, which would pressure the balance sheet and share price in the short term.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: During the Dubai real estate crisis of 2007 to 2010, non-performing loans at UAE banks peaked at around 10 percent, a useful worst-case reference for regional lending stress.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Stress-test method: assume a conservative share of foreign-exposure loans turns non-performing, convert the provision hit to after-tax terms, and compare it with the bank's market value rather than with headline loan size.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Headline risks such as a regional conflict can push a bank's share price down sharply in the short term even when the after-tax earnings hit is small relative to the market value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A bank's real earnings come from the gap between what it pays on deposits, especially current accounts, and what it earns lending to the government and local businesses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Matching fixed-cost deposits with fixed-rate PIBs, and central-bank borrowing with floating PIBs, keeps the bank's margin steady when rates move; the only gap is a six-month repricing lag on the floating side.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Rate-risk check for a bank: match fixed-rate liabilities with fixed-rate government paper and floating borrowings with floating paper; over a one-to-two-year horizon, the spread then stays roughly constant even if rates rise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL's university project is a pure CSR activity with no meaningful effect on earnings growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Only three large banks, HBL, Bank of Punjab and National Bank, do most agricultural financing, and two of those three are government-owned.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Agriculture lending is hard for banks because the farm economy is poorly documented, so entrants must build new systems, such as digital tools to track farm loans, before the segment becomes an earnings contributor.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Floods in Pakistan are coming more frequently, which raises credit risk for banks that lend to farmers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Khushhali Microfinance Bank's equity was about +5 billion rupees in 2022, but heavy losses in later years drove its net worth negative.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A bank in Pakistan must hold net assets of at least about 5 billion rupees, which is why under-capitalised microfinance banks need injections from larger partners.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst benchmarks a single bank against the PSX index: in the bull phases of 1999 to 2007 and 2009 to 2017 the index averaged about 35 percent a year, and a stock must beat that to justify concentrated exposure.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In past bull markets UBL's P/E multiple has typically moved to around 11 to 12 times earnings, which the analyst uses as the reference multiple when projecting a price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Valuation method: start from a chosen future share price, divide by a reference bull-market P/E to get the earnings needed, then work backward to the deposit base and deposit growth rate that would produce those earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'UBL Fair Value Calculation - Is It Still Undervalued?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
